blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Texture interpolation asks what should lie between two textures. Standard methods typically blend pixels or features at corresponding spatial locations, implicitly assuming that co-located elements should be mixed. For unrelated textures, however, this correspondence is arbitrary: a crack at one location has no particular relationship to a fiber at the same location in another image. We study whether this hidden pairing choice is itself a major determinant of interpolation quality. We represent textures as collections of local appearance vectors, or textons, and replace positional pairing with appearance-aware matching while keeping the encoder, representation, and decoder fixed. This isolates the effect of correspondence from changes in model capacity or training. Across texture pairs, appearance-aware matching consistently improves the distributional quality of interpolated midpoints over positional feature blending. Soft matching produces the strongest midpoint statistics, whereas one-to-one assignments yield more balanced transitions and closer agreement with the target endpoint. The same intervention also improves a second pretrained texture interpolator without retraining. These results identify correspondence as a first-class design choice in texture interpolation: meaningful transitions depend not only on how strongly two textures are mixed, but also on which local appearances are mixed with one another.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
What should lie between cracked earth and lined fur? A useful texture
transition forms a plausible material whose local appearance changes with the
interpolation parameter. An RGB cross-fade often leaves two transparent
patterns overlaid. Blending learned features can produce the same failure
( Figure 1 d). Both operations pair elements by spatial index, even
though a crack at one location has no special relationship to the fiber at
that location in an unrelated image.

Interpolation chooses a representation and an association between its
elements. Spatial pairing is useful for registered images. For unregistered
textures, appearance gives a more informative association. We test this
distinction by changing the partner map inside a fixed encoder and decoder
( Figure 1 a–c).

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Julesz proposed that texture perception rests on local elements, textons,
and their statistics ( Julesz, 1981 ) . Parametric models made this
operational by matching joint statistics of wavelet
coefficients ( Portilla & Simoncelli, 2000 ) , and deep variants match the
statistics of convolutional features ( Gatys et al., 2015 ) . CNT makes the
elements explicit as localized Gaussian primitives with appearance
vectors ( Tu et al., 2024 ) . Every such representation ends with a set of
local descriptors, which we call textons, so interpolation has to decide
which textons combine.

blocks.en:
Statistical texture synthesis ranges from wavelet
models ( Portilla & Simoncelli, 2000 ) to deep feature
statistics ( Gatys et al., 2015 ) . Wasserstein texture
barycenters ( Rabin et al., 2012 ) , sliced Wasserstein
losses ( Heitz et al., 2021 ) , and GOTEX ( Houdard et al., 2023 ) already
use transport for synthesis or mixing. Risser (2020) moves
autoencoder features toward their optimal-transport targets and interpolates
between them; we build on this operator and isolate the pairing rule as the
only variable inside a fixed encoder and decoder.
Gaussian feature transforms ( Li et al., 2017 ) , to which our Gaussian
row is related through covariance alignment (see also Huang & Belongie, 2017 ),
and transport on generative latents ( Agustsson et al., 2019 ) also
motivate our distributional controls.
We compare matching rules and their endpoint effects under a shared
representation and renderer, then evaluate the decoded results.
Full-reference texture metrics rest on the premise this paper builds on:
DISTS tolerates texture resampling by comparing spatial statistics of deep
features rather than co-located values ( Ding et al., 2022 ) , and the
information–estimation metric derives a distance from an image prior that
reduces to a second-moment distance for Gaussian priors ( Ohayon et al., 2026 ) .
Both find that low-order statistics of a good representation carry most of a
texture’s perceptual content, which our Gaussian and target-mean rows show
from the operator’s side; our object is an interpolation operator, not a
distance. We systematically vary the pairing rule within a shared frozen
encoder–decoder to separate the effects of appearance information, target
coverage, and matching sharpness; that isolation, not the transport
machinery, is the contribution.

object being matched from the hardness of its matching rule. Related transport
methods preserve content through self-similarity constraints in style
transfer ( Kolkin et al., 2019 ) .

blocks.en: 5 Discussion and Limitations
blocks.zh: 5. 讨论和限制

blocks.en:
The task is a directed
transition under retained source conditioning: a diffuse barycentric map
does not reproduce the target distribution exactly, retaining L A L_{A} does
not guarantee pixelwise preservation of source structure, and a texture
interpolated with itself is not returned unchanged. Periodic textures remain difficult because
local marginals omit phase and long-range organization, and CNT
reconstruction error bounds the outputs ( Section D.6 ). No single
metric establishes that both endpoints are perceptually represented, and
endpoint balance rewards superposition as readily as realism rewards
typicality; the generative comparator uses single outputs
from fixed prompts; no human preference study is included.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
Texture interpolation is a matching problem before it is a blending problem.
Deciding which textons combine, inside a fixed encoder and decoder, improves
midpoints in CNT and in a trained interpolator; soft matching favours
ensemble statistics, one-to-one matching favours balance.

CNT predicts about 101 Gaussian primitives per texture, of
which about 30 carry most of the weight. On 120 pairs we pair the two primitive sets with a Hungarian
assignment under a position cost, an appearance cost, or their mixture, and
either freeze the source layout or let the matched primitives move; the
encoder, primitives, interpolation, and decoder are otherwise those of the
main protocol ( Table 6 ). With a frozen layout the cost is
a null result (KID 0.030 / 0.030 / 0.027 for position /
appearance / mixed; appearance against position +0.0001, CI
[-0.0041,+0.0043]), and reassigning every pairing changes per-image realism by
0.001. With a moving layout, appearance matching is the worst
choice (0.080 against 0.036, Δ \Delta KID +0.0433, CI
[+0.0333,+0.0534]), because look-alike partners are far apart and the moved
primitives superpose. Intervals are paired leave-one-pair-out jackknife,
95% CI. A soft matching of the same primitives reaches
0.016 KID, against 0.019 for the dense operator and
0.030 for every one-to-one rule. The matching’s softness and the
anchoring to the source layout, not the cue used to pair, separate a coherent
intermediate from a superposition.
